clue.text: Sweet women, with it

definitions.meaning: a sweet is a dessert, and this baked dessert has a biscuit base and a soft creamy topping
the slang term for photographs of women with sex appeal, 'it' being the old word for that allure

explanation.surface: A description of someone, perhaps a charming and fashionable lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like 'fashionable', but here 'it' is sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a creamy dessert and glamour photography of alluring women.

clue.text: In which to discuss ambiguous chromatograph, having lost the plot

indicators.note: something open to more than one reading suggests the letters can be arranged in a different order
the long word drops a stretch of its letters

parts.note: a graph is a plot of data

explanation.surface: A scientist's analysing instrument that has gone haywire and lost its plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes GRAPH ('the plot') from CHROMATOGRAPH, leaving CHROMATO, which 'ambiguous' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An online forum is a virtual space where people talk in real time.

clue.text: Florida property?

parts.note: Florida is one of the eastern US states, and a property is a landed holding

explanation.surface: A question about real estate in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: Florida is an E(astern) state, so it is literally an 'E state', and a property with land is also this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed property is called an estate, and Florida is an eastern state.

clue.text: It's certain, the collapse of us bank

indicators.note: the two letters of us fall down and land in a different order

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction that an American bank is sure to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the collapse of' rearranges US to SU. 'us bank' looks like a United States bank; 'bank' is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'surely' expresses confidence that something is without doubt so.

clue.text: Consumer's implement, on it's own no use to cut and paste

definitions.text: Consumer's implement, on it's own no use

parts.note: to chop is to cut
to stick is to paste or glue

explanation.surface: A gripe that a single eating tool is useless when editing text by cutting and pasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut and paste' looks like computer editing, but each verb gives one half. The definition is fair: you need two of these to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a pair of thin sticks used for eating in East Asia, useless singly.

clue.text: Con perpetrated dreadful ordeal where wealth comes easy

indicators.note: a dreadful version of the word is a badly mangled one, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, a con

explanation.surface: A fraud carrying out a terrible ordeal in a place of easy riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' stands first in the clue but its letters come last, after the rearranged ordeal; 'perpetrated' is only a link. The surface's swindler fits the legend of a city of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the fabled city of gold sought by explorers, a byword for easy riches.

clue.text: Peter's free from danger

definitions.meaning: peter is old criminal slang for a strongbox that a burglar might crack
unharmed and out of harm's way

explanation.surface: Someone called Peter has escaped harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name; in thieves' slang it is a strongbox, and safe-crackers were 'petermen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox and the adjective for being out of harm's way share one spelling.

clue.text: One from south touring dives — where I may perform?

definitions.text: One from south touring dives — where I may perform?

parts.note: a tripper is a sightseer, one who goes touring, here round seedy clubs

explanation.surface: A southern tourist visiting sleazy bars asks if they could perform there.
explanation.walkthrough: S (south) comes before TRIPPER, a day-trip tourist; the whole clue then describes the answer, who performs in seedy 'dives'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic dancer who undresses on stage might well perform in seedy clubs.

clue.text: Carp about such a business establishment?

definitions.text: Carp about such a business establishment?

parts.words: Carp about such a business establishment?
parts.note: carp is a fish raised commercially, so the business is all about carp; carp about also suggests complaining

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about a company or institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the verb 'complain'; it is the fish, which is what such an aquaculture business is about.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquaculture business rears fish such as carp commercially in ponds or tanks.

clue.text: Server working from Bray a lot

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are put to work, reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: A waiter who has come from the Thames-side village of Bray, home of famous restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges BRAY A LOT. 'Server' suggests a waiter, apt for Bray, a Berkshire village famous for top restaurants; here it is the boy who assists the priest at the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who assists the priest during Mass is said to serve at the altar.

clue.text: Force the last of you into evening wear

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: formal dress is what people wear in the evening

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A command to push something final into a formal gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last of' gives U, the final letter of 'you', and 'into' puts it inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion, pressure applied by threats, as in 'signed under duress'.

clue.text: Just 38 ot books so severe?

parts.note: Ruth is one of the books of the Old Testament (OT)
the Old Testament has 39 books, so just 38 is one fewer than the full set

explanation.surface: A grumble that a mere 38 Old Testament books seems a harsh selection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Testament (OT) has 39 books, so 'Just 38' of them is the canon with one missing; that one is Ruth, giving RUTH then LESS. 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking mercy or pity makes someone harsh, unsparing and cruel in judgement.

clue.text: Tearaway's confidence trick?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, tear away, meaning pull off forcibly
a swindle or fraud in which someone is cheated

explanation.surface: The scam pulled by a young hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearaway' looks like the noun for a wild youngster, but it is read as the verb phrase 'tear away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling something off forcibly and a swindle that overcharges someone share the same phrase.

clue.text: How I get a lot from the same place

parts.note: at an auction you make an offer to win a lot

explanation.surface: Someone wondering how they collect a lot of something from one source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot' suggests a large amount; at auction it is an item, and how I get one is that I BID. The answer is Latin for 'in the same place', used in references.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in footnotes means a citation repeats the previous source.

clue.text: A host of drinkers or travellers?

definitions.text: A host of drinkers or travellers?

parts.words: A host of drinkers or travellers?
parts.note: not a crowd of people, but the landlord who hosts both those drinking at the bar and those lodging overnight

explanation.surface: A large crowd of drinkers or of travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A host of' looks like 'a large number of'; it means the one who hosts them, a landlord of a pub with rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord of a pub with rooms serves drinks to locals and lodges travellers.

clue.text: Centrepoint of grand act demonstrates it

definitions.meaning: the note at the centre of a grand piano keyboard
the word act has the letter C at its centre, so it shows a C in the middle

explanation.surface: A show at a grand venue's centre that proves something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' is a grand piano, whose middle note is the C nearest its centre; and the word 'act' literally has C in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano note nearest the centre of the keyboard also describes the central letter of 'act'.

clue.text: Secretly zany American

indicators.note: something zany is wildly eccentric, so the letters are thrown into a crazy new order

explanation.surface: A covertly eccentric person from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zany' rearranges AMERICAN. The answer is Latin legal phrasing for proceedings held in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Court hearings held in private, not in open court, are said to be held this way.

clue.text: It's easy to follow duke with one uncultured diver

indicators.note: the easy letters come after the abbreviation for the nobleman

parts.note: 'easy as ABC' is the idiom, so ABC stands for something easy
a hick is an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A nobleman followed by a boorish person, all easy to manage, and a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: D (duke) is followed by ABC, from 'easy as ABC', then HICK. The dabchick, or little grebe, is a small diving water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The little grebe is a small waterbird that dives for its food.

clue.text: About 50% of us from another world

definitions.text: About 50% of us from another world

parts.words: About 50% of us from another world
parts.note: roughly half the human race is male, and seen from another planet we are all inhabitants of our own planet

explanation.surface: Roughly half of us are aliens.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to say half of us are aliens; from an alien's viewpoint, the men among us (about half) are men of our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To aliens in science fiction, humans are people of the third planet from the sun, and about half are male.

clue.text: Call at table for t-bone or sirloin?

definitions.meaning: at the bridge table, a bid proposing play without a trump suit
neither cut of beef is from the rump

explanation.surface: A diner asking for one of two steaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' suggests a dinner order, but it is the bridge table. Split as NOT RUMP, it describes steaks cut from elsewhere on the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge bid for play without a trump suit also reads as 'not rump', fitting other steak cuts.

clue.text: Supporter of final heat noticed climbing mountains

parts.note: a funeral pyre holds up the body during cremation, the final heat

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word goes upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: noticed means seen

explanation.surface: A fan of the final race in a contest, spotted climbing in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns SEEN into NEES. 'final heat' looks like a sporting race, but it is cremation, supported by a funeral pyre.
explanation.definitionFit: This range of high peaks forms the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Relative making ends meet with it

indicators.note: the first and last letters of making come together around the rest, which is what is left once they are dropped

explanation.surface: A family member just about managing financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making ends meet' looks like an idiom for getting by; instead strip the first and last letters, M and G, from 'making' to leave its middle. 'Relative' is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or similar, as relatives are of the same kin.

clue.text: System of exercise: thanks to system of divination, no good running out

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: the letters for no good leave the divination word, running out of it

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese book of changes, used for divination

explanation.surface: Someone crediting a method of fortune-telling for their workout, as nothing good ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks. 'running out' removes NG ('no good') from I CHING, leaving ICHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese martial art practised as slow, flowing exercise.

clue.text: In la Scala, I swig port

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An opera-goer drinking at the famous Milan theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the hidden word, inside 'sCALA, I Swig'. 'port' looks like the drink; it is the French ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the French ferry port facing Dover across the Channel.

clue.text: Excessively well-rewarded football club leading at double

parts.note: FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club
the word at is used twice
FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club
the word at is used twice

explanation.surface: A football club topping the table twice over and getting rich rewards.
explanation.walkthrough: Each letter of FC (Football Club) leads a copy of AT, the word used twice ('double'): F+AT+C+AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is a wealthy executive paid lavishly, often regardless of results.

clue.text: Poet needing half-rotation of fifth state

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the poet's name is turned through 180 degrees, so the letter M flips into a W

parts.note: Walter de la Mare was an English poet

explanation.surface: A poet who needs half of something turned in the fifth state.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifth letter of DE LA MARE is M; given a half-turn (upside down) it becomes W. 'fifth state' looks like one phrase, but 'fifth' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the fifty United States, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Say Mme arcati's neither good nor bad

definitions.meaning: Madame Arcati is the eccentric spiritualist in Noel Coward's play Blithe Spirit, an example of a clairvoyant who contacts the dead

explanation.surface: Someone judging the eccentric spiritualist in Blithe Spirit as merely average.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Arcati is the eccentric spiritualist in Noel Coward's comedy Blithe Spirit; 'Say' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist who contacts the dead and something middling or average share the same word.

clue.text: Time to fly me to the moon?

definitions.text: Time to fly me to the moon?

parts.words: Time to fly me to the moon?
parts.note: the era of rocket travel, when a request to be flown to the moon, as in the Sinatra song, could be granted

explanation.surface: A line from the famous Frank Sinatra song, as if asking when it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly Me to the Moon' is the song; the era when such flights became possible began with the 1960s space race.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of space exploration is when flights to the moon became possible.

clue.text: Put money on second

definitions.meaning: to bet on or financially support
as a verb, to support a motion or person

explanation.surface: Advice to bet on the runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs: to bet on a horse, and to support a motion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagering on a horse and supporting a proposal are both expressed by the same verb.

clue.text: Stingy young women given 50s? Not quite

parts.note: near is an old word for mean with money
misses is a word for girls or unmarried young women

explanation.surface: Mean young ladies passing fifty, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. In cricket, scores in the forties are near misses for a fifty, so the definition is 'not quite 50s'.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow failures fall just short of a target, such as a batter out in the forties.
